_about: Father, Son and Spirit side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings that more than one book shares where the texts speak of the Father, the Son and the Spirit together, of God as one, and of each distinctly, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme's own outline cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit named together

Gospels & Acts: baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit
The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the Holy One to be born will be called the Son of God
Exalted, then, to the right hand of God, He has received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit
full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God
God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power
The letters: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you
There are different gifts, but the same Spirit
There are different ministries, but the same Lord
There are different ways of working, but the same God works all things in all people
There is one body and one Spirit
one Lord, one faith, one baptism
one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all
through Him we both have access to the Father by one Spirit
according to the foreknowledge of God the Father and sanctified by the Spirit for obedience to Jesus Christ
keep yourselves in the love of God as you await the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ
in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God
no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus be cursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit
it is God who establishes both us and you in Christ
put His Spirit in our hearts as a pledge of what is to come
a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit
by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me
brothers who are loved by the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning to be saved by the sanctification of the Spirit
This is the Spirit He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior
the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God
By this you will know the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God

rows.alike: Each passage names the Spirit together with one or more of God, the Father, the Most High, the Lord, Jesus, Christ or the Son of God: "in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 28:19), "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit" (2 Corinthians 13:14), "the same Spirit", "the same Lord", "the same God" (1 Corinthians 12:4-6).
rows.different: The order differs: Matthew 28:19 has "the Father ... the Son ... the Holy Spirit", "baptizing them"; 2 Corinthians 13:14 begins with "the Lord Jesus Christ"; 1 Corinthians 12:4-6 and Ephesians 4:4-6 begin with the Spirit ("the same Spirit", "the same Lord", "the same God"; "one Spirit", "one Lord", "one God and Father of all"). In Luke 1:35 an angel speaks of "the Most High" and "the Son of God"; Acts 7:55 tells what Stephen, "full of the Holy Spirit", saw: "the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God".

rows.title: A voice: “This is My beloved Son”, and the Spirit descending like a dove

Gospels & Acts: He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him
a voice from heaven said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased!”
He saw the heavens breaking open and the Spirit descending on Him like a dove
a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”
the Holy Spirit descended on Him in a bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”
I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove and resting on Him
I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God
a voice from the cloud said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to Him!”
a voice came from the cloud: “This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him!”
a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!”
The letters: He received honor and glory from God the Father when the voice came to Him from the Majestic Glory, saying, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

rows.alike: A voice says "This is My beloved Son" or "You are My beloved Son" (Matthew 3:17, Mark 1:11, Luke 3:22, Matthew 17:5, Mark 9:7, 2 Peter 1:17); each of the four Gospels tells of the Spirit descending "like a dove" (Matthew 3:16, Mark 1:10, Luke 3:22, John 1:32).
rows.different: In the voice's words Matthew 3:17 has "This is My beloved Son", Mark 1:11 and Luke 3:22 "You are My beloved Son"; Luke adds "in a bodily form"; in John it is John who says "I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove" and "this is the Son of God". The voice "from the cloud" adds "Listen to Him!", and Luke 9:35 has "whom I have chosen"; 2 Peter 1:17 says the voice came "from the Majestic Glory" and that He "received honor and glory from God the Father".

rows.title: There is no other; no God besides Me

The Law & history: the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him
the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth below; there is no other
See now that I am He; there is no God besides Me
Indeed, there is no one besides You!
there is none like You, and there is no God but You

so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God. There is no other!
there is none like You, and there is no God but You
there is no other but this one here
Psalms & wisdom: For who is God besides the LORD?
The Prophets: Is there any God but Me? There is no other Rock; I know not one.
I am the LORD, and there is no other; there is no God but Me

They will confess to you: ‘God is indeed with you, and there is no other; there is no other God.'

who says to herself, ‘I am, and there is none besides me.
you told yourself, ‘I am, and there is none besides me.'
This carefree city that dwells securely, that thinks to herself: “I am it, and there is none besides me,”

rows.alike: Each, the asterisked cells aside, says there is none besides the LORD, in words such as "the LORD is God; there is no other besides Him" (Deuteronomy 4:35), "For who is God besides the LORD?" (Psalm 18:31), "I am the LORD, and there is no other" (Isaiah 45:5).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 4:35 and 1 Kings 8:60 say it so that people "would know" or "may know"; 1 Samuel 2:2, 2 Samuel 7:22 and 1 Chronicles 17:20 address the LORD as "You" ("there is no one besides You", "there is no God but You"); in Deuteronomy 32:39, Isaiah 44-46, Hosea 13:4 and Joel 2:27 it is in the first person ("there is no God besides Me", "there is no God but Me"); Isaiah 45:14 puts it in the mouths of those who "will confess to you". Isaiah 47:8 and Zephaniah 2:15 give the words "there is none besides me" to one who "says to herself" and to a "carefree city". 1 Samuel 21:9 has "there is no other but this one here" of Goliath's sword.

rows.title: The only God; the true God

The Law & history: Israel has been without the true God
The Prophets: But the LORD is the true God; He is the living God and eternal King
Gospels & Acts: the glory that comes from the only God
that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent
The letters: to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ!
you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God
Now to the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever
to the only God our Savior be glory, majesty, dominion, and authority through Jesus Christ our Lord
so that we may know Him who is true; and we are in Him who is true-in His Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life.

rows.alike: Each speaks of God as the only God or the true God, in words such as "the LORD is the true God" (Jeremiah 10:10), "the only true God" (John 17:3), "the living and true God" (1 Thessalonians 1:9).
rows.different: John 17:3 says of eternal life "that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent". Romans 16:27 and Jude 1:25 give glory to "the only" God "through Jesus Christ"; 1 Thessalonians 1:9 sets "the living and true God" against "idols"; Jeremiah 10:10 adds "the living God and eternal King". 1 John 5:20 has "Him who is true", "His Son Jesus Christ" and "He is the true God and eternal life."

rows.title: The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ; “My Father ... My God”

Gospels & Acts: I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.
The letters: glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is forever worthy of praise, knows that I am not lying
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father
We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ!
one God and Father of all
our God and Father your work of faith, your labor of love, and your enduring hope in our Lord Jesus Christ
our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus
before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus
Revelation: priests to His God and Father

rows.alike: Each pairs "God" with "Father": "the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ" (2 Corinthians 1:3), "His God and Father" (Revelation 1:6), "My Father ... My God" (John 20:17), "one God and Father of all" (Ephesians 4:6).
rows.different: In John 20:17 Jesus speaks of "My Father" and "My God", then "your Father" and "your God", in a message for "My brothers". Ephesians 1:17 has "the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father"; Colossians 1:3 "God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ". In the letters it is in a call to "glorify" (Romans 15:6), a blessing ("Blessed be"), a thanksgiving ("We always thank God"), and in 2 Corinthians 11:31 it is the One who "knows that I am not lying". Ephesians 4:6 has "one God and Father of all"; 1 Thessalonians 1:3, 3:11 and 3:13 have "our God and Father" with "our Lord Jesus" in the same verse.

Revelation: Grace and peace to you from Him who is and was and is to come, and from the seven spirits before His throne
and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness

rows.alike: Each is a greeting of grace or peace, and most send it "from" God, as "our Father" or "the Father", and from the Lord Jesus Christ, Christ Jesus or Jesus Christ: "Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ" (Romans 1:7), word for word in 1 Corinthians 1:3, 2 Corinthians 1:2, Galatians 1:3, Ephesians 1:2, Philippians 1:2, 2 Thessalonians 1:2 and Philemon 1:3.
rows.different: 1 and 2 Timothy and 2 John add "mercy"; 2 John adds "the Son of the Father"; Titus has "Christ Jesus our Savior"; Colossians 1:2 has "from God our Father" alone; Ephesians 6:23 sends "Peace ... and love with faith"; 2 Peter 1:2 has "through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord". Revelation 1:4-5 sends it "from Him who is and was and is to come, and from the seven spirits before His throne" "and from Jesus Christ". 1 Thessalonians 1:1 puts the church "in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ" before "Grace and peace to you", and 1 Peter 1:2 names "God the Father", "the Spirit" and "Jesus Christ" before "Grace and peace be yours in abundance".

rows.title: Whoever knows, honors or has the Son has the Father as well

Gospels & Acts: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.
If you had known Me, you would know My Father as well.
Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father.
Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well.
they have seen and hated both Me and My Father
The letters: This is the antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son.
Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father, but whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well.
Whoever remains in His teaching has both the Father and the Son.

rows.alike: Each speaks in one saying of "Me" or "the Son" and of "My Father" or "the Father": "If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well" (John 8:19), "Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well" (John 15:23), "whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well" (1 John 2:23).
rows.different: In John the words are "Me" and "My Father", in 8:19 answering "Where is Your Father?" and in 14:9 Philip's "Show us the Father"; John 5:23 adds "the Father who sent Him". 1 John and 2 John speak of "the Son" and "the Father", with "denies", "confesses" and "remains in His teaching"; 1 John 2:22 says of one "who denies the Father and the Son", "This is the antichrist".

rows.title: I am in the Father and the Father is in Me; in the Son and in the Father

Gospels & Acts: the Father is in Me, and I am in the Father
Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me?
Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me

The letters: you will also remain in the Son and in the Father
To the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
To the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
we are in Him who is true-in His Son Jesus Christ

rows.alike: Each uses "in" with the Father, God or "Him who is true", and with the Son, Jesus Christ or the Lord: "I am in the Father and the Father is in Me" (John 14:10), "remain in the Son and in the Father" (1 John 2:24), "in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Thessalonians 1:1), "in Him who is true-in His Son Jesus Christ" (1 John 5:20).
rows.different: In John 10:38, 14:10-11 and 14:20 the speaker says "I am in the Father" or "I am in My Father"; John 14:20 goes on "and you are in Me, and I am in you", and 10:38 and 14:11 tie it to "the works". In 1 John 2:24 and 5:20 it is said of "you" and "we" ("you will also remain", "we are in Him"), and in 1 and 2 Thessalonians of "the church".

rows.title: The Word, and what was with God and with the Father

Gospels & Acts: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

rows.alike: Each speaks of "the Word", or of what was with God or the Father "in the beginning", "from the beginning" or "before the world existed": "the Word was with God" (John 1:1), "the glory I had with You before the world existed" (John 17:5), "the eternal life that was with the Father" (1 John 1:2).
rows.different: John 1:1 says "the Word was with God, and the Word was God", and 1:14 "The Word became flesh"; John 17:5 is spoken to "Father", asking "glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed". 1 John 1:1-2 speaks of "the Word of life" and of "the eternal life that was with the Father and was revealed to us". In Revelation 19:13 "The Word of God" is the name of one who "is dressed in a robe dipped in blood".

rows.title: The Spirit of your Father, of Jesus, of Christ, of His Son

Gospels & Acts: the Spirit of your Father speaking through you

The letters: if the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ

rows.alike: Each names the Spirit "of" the Father or "of" the Son: "the Spirit of your Father" (Matthew 10:20), "the Spirit of Jesus" (Acts 16:7), "the Spirit of Christ" (Romans 8:9), "the Spirit of His Son" (Galatians 4:6).
rows.different: Romans 8:9 has "the Spirit of God" and "the Spirit of Christ" in one verse, and 8:11 "the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead"; Galatians 4:6 says "God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts". In Matthew 10:20 "it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you"; in Acts 16:7 "the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them" to enter Bithynia; in 1 Peter 1:11 "the Spirit of Christ in them" "predicted the sufferings of Christ".

rows.alike: Each says the Father or God "sent" the Son: "the Father who sent Me" (John 5:37), "God sent His Son" (Galatians 4:4), "the Father has sent His Son" (1 John 4:14).
rows.different: In John it is mostly said in the first person, "sent Me", and with what is said or done: "has commanded Me what to say", "testifies about Me", "I live because of the Father"; in John 20:21 "so also I am sending you". The letters say it of "His Son" and add what for: "born of a woman, born under the law", "in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin", "as the atoning sacrifice for our sins", "to be the Savior of the world"; John 3:17 has "not ... to condemn the world, but to save the world through Him".

rows.title: His one and only Son

rows.different: John 1:18 has the one and only Son "at the Father's side" who "has made Him known"; John 3:16 says God "gave" Him, 1 John 4:9 that God "sent" Him; John 3:18 speaks of believing "in the name of God's one and only Son". Hebrews 11:17 says "his one and only son" of Isaac, whom Abraham was "ready to offer".

rows.title: No one knows ... except

Gospels & Acts: No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him

rows.alike: Five of these say "no one knows" and then name who does: "no one knows the Father except the Son" (Matthew 11:27), "no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God" (1 Corinthians 2:11), "No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father" (Matthew 24:36).
rows.different: Matthew 11:27 and Luke 10:22 say it of the Father and the Son each knowing the other, and add "and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him"; John 10:15, which does not say "no one", has "the Father knows Me and I know the Father". Matthew 24:36 and Mark 13:32 say it of "that day or hour", with "not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son". 1 Corinthians 2:11 sets it beside "the thoughts of man" known by "his own spirit within him".

rows.different: John 10:17 gives a reason: "that I lay down My life in order to take it up again"; John 17:24, addressed to the "Father", says "before the foundation of the world"; John 15:9 goes on "so have I loved you"; John 5:20 adds "shows Him all He does". Colossians 1:13 speaks of being brought "into the kingdom of His beloved Son".
